name: Isometric World
summary: A floating isometric factory: your pipeline as a belt, Pulse as a teal glass layer, one coral cube diverted to a human.
look: Airy radial background, white floating platform on a 2:1 isometric grid lit from the top-left in three tones, a dark belt with white cubes, a translucent teal layer with a tiny robot and flat pinned labels.

components.name: Floating tile platform
components.role: white top, two darker side tones, 2:1 grid lines, teal edge

components.name: Pipeline belt
components.role: dark band carrying white metric cubes — the customer’s existing system

components.name: Glass audit layer
components.role: translucent teal slab hovering over the belt: Pulse, never in the way

components.name: Watcher robot
components.role: small teal cube with two eyes and a coral antenna light (= agent running)

components.name: Scan gate
components.role: teal arch with a light plane that reads every cube on the beat

components.name: Pinned label
components.role: flat camera-facing card with a dashed leader to its object; coral for the anomaly

motion.name: Iso glide
motion.how: camera slides along the 30° axes only (never rotates), sine.inOut over 2 bars (4 s)

motion.name: Build-up drop
motion.how: tile rows fall 40 px + fade, back.out(1.4) 0.35 s, one row per half-beat (0.25 s at 120 BPM)

motion.name: Divert
motion.how: arm rotates 0 → 35° in 0.12 s (steps feel) on the downbeat; coral cube slides the chute with power2.in 0.5 s

story: Hook: a cluttered isometric desk with screens and paper stacks, pinned labels for 38 dashboards, p95 212 ms, error rate 0.4 %. Reveal: the platform builds on the drop, a teal glass layer lands over the belt with the watcher robot, and the Acme Pulse lockup sets. Proof: cubes pass the scan gate; one exits coral — Checkout conversion −18% since 09:42 after deploy #2231 — and is diverted to the review desk with a Roll back button. CTA: bird’s-eye miniature with all lights green, lockup, tagline and Start free.
adapt: Model your customer’s workflow as a belt of objects (tickets, orders, builds, invoices), put your product as a layer or station above it, and divert exactly one object to a human.

references.note: Monument Valley: strict 30° isometric grid as a design rule

fit.risk: Illustration-heavy and slow to produce; small labels get lost on phones.
